1.q: How does a large language model produce an answer?
o: It looks up the answer in a database
It predicts the next small piece of text (token), again and again
It copies the best website in real time
1.why: LLMs generate text one token at a time, based on patterns learned in training and whatever is in the context window.

o: When the AI refuses to answer
A confident-sounding answer that's wrong or made up
When the AI repeats your question
1.why: Because models predict likely text, they can produce plausible but false facts. Check what matters.

1.q: What's the best way to get current information, like today's prices?
o: Ask the model to try harder
Turn on web search and ask for sources
1.why: Models only know their training data plus what's in the context window. Search brings in current pages you can check.

1.q: Which is safe to paste into an AI tool?
1.why: Replace names and numbers with placeholders, then add the real details yourself afterwards.

1.q: When is it OK to clone someone's voice?
o: When it's your own voice, or you have written permission
1.why: Cloning without consent is forbidden by every major voice platform and illegal in many places.

2.q: Which part of a prompt do people skip most, even though it matters most?
2.why: The model can't guess your business, audience or goal. Context is what turns a generic answer into a useful one.

o: Showing 2–3 examples of the input and output you want
2.why: Examples show the pattern, and the model copies it reliably.

2.q: Why wrap a pasted document in tags like <contract>…</contract>?
o: It separates your material from your instructions
It's required by every AI tool
It hides the document from the AI
2.why: Clear boundaries stop the model confusing the text you pasted with what you asked it to do.

2.q: A draft sounds too salesy. Which follow-up works best?
o: Start a new chat with the same prompt
'Rewrite it as if a friend is recommending it, and keep the structure of the second paragraph.'
2.why: Specific follow-ups give specific results. Vague ones give random ones.

2.q: When does a prompt template earn a place in your library?
o: As soon as you write it
After it works on two real tasks without heavy editing
2.why: Only tested templates save time. Untested ones just move the work around.

3.q: What is a Claude Project for?
o: A workspace whose instructions and files every chat starts with
3.why: Put your context, voice and key files in a project once, and every chat inside it uses them.

3.q: What is a custom GPT in ChatGPT?
o: A mini-assistant with fixed instructions, knowledge files and optional tools
A prompt shortcut on your keyboard
3.why: Build one for a repeated job, such as writing menu descriptions, and reuse or share it.

3.q: Which tool is search-first and gives sources with every answer?
3.why: Perplexity is useful for quick research and for fact-checking claims from other assistants.

3.q: How do you get AI writing that sounds like you?
o: Give it your style guide plus your own rough notes, then edit the draft
3.why: Starting from your own notes and voice guide keeps the result yours.

3.q: Why ask the model to quote the exact sentence from a source?
o: To check the claim is actually in the source
3.why: If the model can't find the quote, the claim may not be in the source.

4.q: What makes a set of AI images look like one photoshoot?
o: Using a different tool for each image
Changing every part of the prompt each time
Reusing the same style suffix (style, lighting, colours, ratio)
Adding more emojis to the prompt
4.why: Fix the style words, use reference images and keep one aspect ratio.

4.q: AI voiceover sounds robotic. What's usually the cause?
o: The script: long sentences and no natural pauses
The voice model is too new
4.why: Write for the ear: short sentences, punctuation for pauses, numbers written as spoken.

4.q: Why do professionals prefer image-to-video over text-to-video?
o: It gives more control and consistency
4.why: Starting from a strong image locks in the look, so you only describe the motion.

4.q: What's the best practice for camera movement in an AI clip?
o: Combine an orbit, pan and zoom in one shot
4.why: Combining several moves often produces warped results.

4.q: About how many spoken words fit in 30 seconds of voiceover?
4.why: Lock the voiceover first, then generate shots to fit it, so you waste fewer credits.

4.q: What do you need before making an AI avatar of a real person?
4.why: Never make an avatar of anyone without consent, and label realistic AI content where platforms require it.

5.q: In a web app, which part checks passwords and saves data securely?
5.why: Anything you can't trust the browser with runs on the server, in the backend.

o: Keeping settings and secret keys out of the code
5.why: Secrets live in hosting settings (and .env.local locally), never in GitHub.

5.q: What does row level security (RLS) do in Supabase?
o: Makes the database refuse to show one user's rows to another
5.why: RLS protects data even if the frontend has a bug.

5.q: Which key must never appear in frontend code?
5.why: The secret key bypasses security rules. The publishable key is designed for the browser because RLS protects the data.

o: A project memory file Claude Code reads at the start of every session
5.why: Put the project's purpose, stack, commands and rules in it, and every session starts informed.

o: An open standard for connecting AI apps to tools and data
5.why: Think USB-C for AI: one standard plug between AI apps and the tools they use.

6.q: An AI step inside an automation should output…
o: An exactly defined format, such as one label, with a fallback when unsure
6.why: It runs unattended, so be precise: exact labels, examples and an 'if unsure' rule.

6.q: What should come before an AI agent sends, pays for, deletes or publishes anything?
6.why: Start agents read-only or draft-only, and keep a person in the loop for anything that can't be undone.

6.q: How should you price AI-powered services?
o: By how fast the AI made it
By the value and time saved for the client
6.why: If you save a business 10 hours a month, your fee should reflect that value.

6.q: What's the strongest first pitch to a potential client?
o: A long list of tools you know
A finished sample made for that specific business
6.why: A sample made for them beats any description of what you could do.
